confirmedRules.then: Die Anzeige ist eine Zeichenkette mit Komma und Minuszeichen.
confirmedRules.parameters: Rundung auf Tausendstel über Math.round (mathkit.js:9). Minuszeichen U+2212 (mathkit.js:6). Klammern nur bei negativen Werten (mathkit.js:11).
edgeCases: Die Rundung ist bei genau halben Tausendsteln asymmetrisch, weil Math.round(−2000,5) auf −2000 rundet: fmt(−2.0005) ergibt „−2“, fmt(2.0005) ergibt „2,001“.
fmt(−0.0001) ergibt „−0“, weil das Minuszeichen vor der Rundung gesetzt wird.
Die Anzeige rundet, die Prüfung nicht (siehe Regel zu numerischen Antworten).
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Rundung bei halben Tausendsteln ist asymmetrisch: −2,0005 wird zu −2, aber 2,0005 wird zu 2,001 (mathkit.js:9). Außerdem entsteht bei kleinen negativen Werten die Anzeige „−0“.

confirmedRules.name: Zufällige ganze Zahl im Bereich, Grenzen eingeschlossen
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Eine Zufallszahl wird so gezogen, dass alle Ganzzahlen von a bis b gleich wahrscheinlich sind, beide Grenzen eingeschlossen.
confirmedRules.when: rnd wird aufgerufen.
confirmedRules.then: Es kommt eine Zufallszahl aus dem Bereich zurück.
confirmedRules.parameters: Formel a + floor(Zufall × (b − a + 1)) (mathkit.js:5).
edgeCases: Ist a größer als b, z. B. rnd(5, 3), liegt das Ergebnis bei 4 oder 5 und damit außerhalb des angegebenen Bereichs.
Dezimalgrenzen werden nicht abgerundet: rnd(1.5, 3) liefert 1,5, 2,5 oder 3,5. Der Wert 3,5 liegt über der Obergrenze.

confirmedRules.name: Zufällige Animations-Konfetti: Lebensdauer und Entfernung
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Bei einem Anlass werden 46 bunte Papierstücke eingeblendet, die fallen und nach 5,2 Sekunden wieder entfernt werden.
confirmedRules.given: confetti() wird ohne Argument aufgerufen.
confirmedRules.when: Die Funktion läuft.
confirmedRules.then: Die Stücke verschwinden nach spätestens 5,2 Sekunden.
confirmedRules.parameters: Anzahl 46 (confetti.js:4). Sechs Farben (confetti.js:1). Position 0–100 vw (confetti.js:8). Fallzeit 2–4 s (confetti.js:10). Verzögerung 0–0,6 s (confetti.js:11). Entfernung nach 5200 ms (confetti.js:13).
edgeCases: Die Entfernung nach 5,2 s liegt nach dem spätesten Ende der Animation (0,6 + 4 = 4,6 s), also wird nichts zu früh gelöscht.
Bei reduzierter Bewegung blendet core/styles/base.css:103 die Klasse .cf aus. Die Stücke werden dann trotzdem erzeugt und nach 5,2 s entfernt.
core/js/shell.js:48 entfernt übrig gebliebene .cf-Knoten zusätzlich (nur zur Auflösung der Referenz gelesen).

confirmedRules.name: Minou-Stimmung wählt das Gesicht, unbekannte Stimmung wird zu „fröhlich“
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Minou hat vier Stimmungen (fröhlich, jubelnd, traurig, nachdenklich). Die Stimmung bestimmt Augen und Mund. Eine unbekannte oder fehlende Stimmung ergibt fröhlich.
confirmedRules.given: mascot() ohne Argument oder mit einer unbekannten Stimmung, z. B. „verwirrt“.
confirmedRules.when: Das Maskottchen wird gezeichnet.
confirmedRules.then: Es wird eine der vier Stimmungen gezeichnet.
confirmedRules.parameters: Stimmungen happy (Standard), cheer, sad, hmm (mascot.js:4-16). Fallback EYES.happy und MOUTH.happy (mascot.js:19).
edgeCases: Eine ungültige Stimmung wird stillschweigend zu happy, es gibt keine Warnung.
Die Stimmung wird nur beim Zeichnen gelesen. Es gibt keine Übergänge in dieser Datei.
Welches Ereignis welche Stimmung setzt, steht nicht in dieser Datei.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Welche Ereignisse sollen Minou in welche Stimmung versetzen (z. B. jubelnd bei einem Stern, traurig bei einer falschen Antwort, nachdenklich bei Hinweisen)?

confirmedRules.name: Boss unlock: every unit needs at least one star
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The final boss (Endgegner) opens only after every unit has at least one star, unless the app defines its own unlock rule.
confirmedRules.given: App progress with star counts per unit; the app config either has no bossUnlocked function or has one.
confirmedRules.when: The home screen is drawn, or the player presses the boss start button.
confirmedRules.then: The boss counts as open when every unit has stars > 0 (or when config.bossUnlocked(ctx) returns true). When closed, the boss button is disabled with the label 'Noch gesperrt' (core/js/views/home.js:46-46), and the action handler ignores the click (core/js/shell.js:132-132).
confirmedRules.parameters: Threshold: stars > 0 per unit, no minimum star count. Override: config.bossUnlocked(ctx) (core/js/shell.js:43). Boss card is shown only if config.rounds.boss exists (core/js/views/home.js:28, 46).
edgeCases: An empty unit list makes every() return true, so the boss opens.
If the app has no boss round, the boss card is hidden entirely regardless of progress.

confirmedRules.name: Daily XP goal of 30 XP
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Each calendar day has a goal of 30 XP. Progress toward it is shown capped at 100 percent, and the app celebrates once the goal is reached.
confirmedRules.given: profile.day holds today's date and the XP earned today.
confirmedRules.when: The home screen or the result screen is shown.
confirmedRules.then: Today's XP equals profile.day.xp if profile.day.d is today, otherwise 0 (core/js/profile.js:37). Ring ratio = min(1, xp / 30). Ring label shows min(xp, 30) of 30. At xp >= 30 the text is 'Geschafft. Du bist heute fertig.', otherwise 'Eine kurze Runde bringt dich nah ran.' (core/js/views/home.js:56-57). Result screen shows 'Tagesziel geschafft!' or 'Tagesziel: noch (30 - xp) XP' with a bar of min(100, xp / 30 * 100) percent (core/js/views/result.js:31-33).
confirmedRules.parameters: GOAL = 30 XP (core/js/profile.js:5). Day = local calendar date (core/js/profile.js:22-23).
edgeCases: On a new day the daily XP shows 0 while total XP is kept.
Motivation line (core/js/views/home.js:11-16): 0 XP gives a random encouraging line; 1 to 29 XP gives 'Noch N XP bis zum Tagesziel'; 30 or more gives 'Tagesziel geschafft. Alles ab jetzt ist Bonus.'

confirmedRules.name: Level thresholds and XP progress bar
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Total XP maps to a level, and the header bar shows how far the player is between the current level and the next one.
confirmedRules.given: profile.xp, the total XP across apps.
confirmedRules.when: The header is rendered (every screen, and after each change).
confirmedRules.then: level = highest n with xp >= T(n), where T(n) = 30 * n * (n - 1) (core/js/profile.js:29-33). Bar percent = round((xp - T(n)) / (T(n+1) - T(n)) * 100). Shown as 'Niveau n' and 'xp XP'. The level title from TITLES is used as tooltip (core/js/profile.js:35).
confirmedRules.parameters: T(n) = 30*n*(n-1): level 2 starts at 60 XP, level 3 at 180, level 4 at 360, level 5 at 600. Level titles: Neuling, Entdecker, Könner, Profi, Meister, Expert, Legende (core/js/profile.js:9). Levels beyond 7 reuse the last title.
edgeCases: Example: 90 XP gives Niveau 2 with a bar at 25 percent.
The level-up line appears on the result screen only when rounds.js sets levelUp (core/js/views/result.js:10-10).

confirmedRules.name: Practice streak with one grace day
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The day streak shown in the header survives one skipped day; after two skipped days it shows zero.
confirmedRules.given: profile.lastDay (date of last practice) and profile.streak.
confirmedRules.when: The header is drawn.
confirmedRules.then: Shown value = profile.streak if the day difference between lastDay and today is at most 2, otherwise 0 (core/js/profile.js:40-41). The stored streak is not reset here; it is reset on the next practice (touchStreak, core/js/profile.js:44-46, outside the listed files).
confirmedRules.parameters: Grace rule: difference <= 2 days (one missed day allowed). No practice ever (lastDay empty) gives 0.
edgeCases: Practice yesterday (difference 1) or the day before yesterday (difference 2): streak shown.
Difference 3 or more: 0 shown although the stored value remains until the next practice.

confirmedRules.name: Unit becomes due for refresh after 3 days
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A unit with at least one star is marked 'Zeit zum Auffrischen' once it has not been practised for 3 days.
confirmedRules.given: The unit has stars > 0, and app.last[unit] holds the date of the last practice.
confirmedRules.when: The home screen draws the learning path.
confirmedRules.then: The badge 'Zeit zum Auffrischen' appears on the unit node. The same condition drives the training recommendation (rule 'Training recommendation') and the refresh bonus (rule 'Refreshing a due unit').
confirmedRules.parameters: DUE_DAYS = 3 (core/js/profile.js:12). Due when the day difference from the last practice is at least 3 (core/js/profile.js:79-81).
edgeCases: A unit with 0 stars is never due.
A unit without a last-practice date is never due.
Exactly 3 days counts as due.

Unit lifecycle: not started (0 stars), then learned (>= 1 star), then due (>= 3 days since last practice), then refreshed (a new round sets the last date again; done in core/js/rounds.js, outside the listed files).

confirmedRules.name: Training recommendation: due first, then weakest unit
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The home screen recommends one unit to practise: the oldest due unit first, otherwise the unit with the lowest last accuracy below 90 percent.
confirmedRules.given: app.last, app.acc and app.stars per unit.
confirmedRules.when: The home screen is drawn.
confirmedRules.then: If any unit is due, recommend the one practised longest ago, with reason 'Zeit zum Auffrischen'. Otherwise, among units with a stored accuracy below 0.9 and fewer than 3 stars, recommend the lowest accuracy, with reason 'Hier ist noch Luft nach oben'. If none qualifies, no training card is shown. The button 'Jetzt trainieren' starts a lesson round for that unit (core/js/shell.js:133-133). Selection logic: core/js/profile.js:88-97, outside the listed files.
confirmedRules.parameters: Accuracy threshold 0.9 (90 percent). Star cap: stars < 3 for the weak-unit branch.
edgeCases: A due unit beats a weaker unit, even if the weaker one has lower accuracy.
Units with 3 stars are never recommended as weak.
Only units with a numeric stored accuracy are considered.
The card text promises 10 bonus XP for refreshing (core/js/views/home.js:31), which matches core/js/rounds.js:19-21.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Citation was corrected by referee (The cited lines home.js:29-31 do not implement the selection rule. They call weakestUnit(app, config.units) (line 29) and render its returned reason and unit into the 'Gezieltes Training' card with the 'Jetzt trainieren' button (lines 30-32). The rule's behavior is implemented in core/js/profile.js:88-95, which the rule's own Specification names as the selection logic. That code matches the rule: (1) units with isDue (stars > 0, last practised >= DUE_DAYS = 3 days ago) are filtered, then sorted so the oldest is first (dayDiff(last[b], last[a]) yields oldest-first), with reason 'Zeit zum Auffrischen' (line 90); (2) otherwise units with a numeric acc < 0.9 and stars < 3 are sorted by ascending acc, the lowest is returned with reason 'Hier ist noch Luft nach oben' (lines 91-94); (3) null when nothing qualifies, and home.js:30-32 then renders no card. The rule is therefore substantively correct; only the citation points at the consumer rather than the implementation. No instruction-shaped text found in either cited region, and no credential values involved.) — confirm core/js/profile.js:88-95 is the authoritative implementation.

confirmedRules.name: Collection album card tier from stars
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Each unit with a card has a collectible card. It is locked with no stars and becomes Bronze, Silber or Gold with 1, 2 or 3 stars.
confirmedRules.given: The unit has a card, and app.stars[unit] holds its star count.
confirmedRules.when: The home screen is drawn.
confirmedRules.then: 0 stars: card labelled 'Gesperrt', titled 'Geheimkarte', with a hint to finish the unit. 1 star: Bronze. 2 stars: Silber. 3 stars: Gold. Earned cards show the card name and fact. The album section is hidden if no unit has a card.
confirmedRules.parameters: Tiers 0 to 3 (medal labels in core/js/views/home.js:34-34).
edgeCases: Units without a card are skipped.
Stars are lost only through a full reset of the app (see the reset rule).
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Bestätigen Sie die Zuordnung 1 Stern = Bronze, 2 = Silber, 3 = Gold für die Sammelkarten. Der Test prüft nur 2 Sterne = Silber.

confirmedRules.name: Trophy earned state and newly earned trophies
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A trophy shows as earned once it is recorded for the app. Trophies earned in the last round are listed on the result screen.
confirmedRules.given: app.badges[id] is set when a trophy is earned; result.newBadges comes from the round evaluation.
confirmedRules.when: The home or result screen is drawn.
confirmedRules.then: Home: the 'got' style is applied when app.badges[id] is truthy. Result: a 'Neue Trophäen' block appears only if newBadges is not empty (core/js/views/result.js:9-9 and 33-33).
confirmedRules.parameters: Earning logic is in core/js/rounds.js:45-46 (outside the listed files): newBadges = trophies not yet earned whose when(state, result) is true; those are then flagged as earned.
edgeCases: Already earned trophies are not repeated on the result screen.
A full app reset clears all trophies (see the reset rule).

confirmedRules.name: Result headline, text and celebration by outcome
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: The result screen picks its headline and explanation from the round outcome. For a normal round the headline depends on stars earned, and a celebration fires for strong results.
confirmedRules.given: Round result: failed flag, mode, stars, second-try count, goalHit flag.
confirmedRules.when: A round finishes.
confirmedRules.then: Failed: headline 'Knapp daneben' with encouragement to read the theory. Otherwise headline = resultTitles[stars - 1] (index at least 0): 'Geschafft!' for 1 star, 'Sehr gut!' for 2, 'Perfekt!' for 3. Text by mode: boss 'Endgegner besiegt. 50 Bonus-XP gehören dir.'; quick 'Kurze Runde, echter Fortschritt.'; refresh 'Aufgefrischt! ... 10 Bonus-XP'; otherwise 'Seite geschafft ...' (core/js/views/result.js:20-22). If not failed and relearned > 0, the count of second-try correct answers is appended (core/js/views/result.js:23-23). Celebration (confetti) if goalHit, or blitz with score >= 10, or (not failed and (boss or stars >= 2)) (core/js/views/result.js:34-34). Stars come from starsFor (core/js/profile.js:76, outside the listed files): failed 0, accuracy >= 90 percent gives 3, >= 70 percent gives 2, otherwise 1.
confirmedRules.parameters: Star thresholds 70 and 90 percent (core/js/profile.js:76). Title words from core/js/shell.js:26-26. Mood 'cheer' at 3 stars.
edgeCases: A failed round can still celebrate if it reached the daily goal (goalHit).
Mood 'hmm' for failed rounds.
Blitz uses its own copy (see the Blitz praise rule).

Display difference: the blitz result shows the x-multiplier of the best combo (core/js/views/result.js:16-16), while other modes show the raw best combo count labelled 'längste Serie' (core/js/views/result.js:25-25).
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: Combo display differs by mode: blitz shows a multiplier (x N) for the best combo, other modes show the raw streak length. Confirm this is intended.

confirmedRules.name: Blitz praise threshold at 10 correct answers
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: In the 45-second Blitz, 10 or more correct answers earn the praise title and a cheer. Fewer gives 'Zeit um'.
confirmedRules.given: Round mode is blitz; score is the number of correct answers.
confirmedRules.when: A Blitz round ends.
confirmedRules.then: score >= 10: title 'Blitzschnell!' (words.blitzTitle), mood 'cheer', confetti. Otherwise: title 'Zeit um', mood 'happy', no confetti. Subtext shows the score and the best score app.best.blitz (already updated before rendering, core/js/shell.js:102-106).
confirmedRules.parameters: Threshold 10 correct answers. Round length 45 seconds appears only as text (core/js/views/result.js:14-14); the timer lives in core/js/blitz.js, not read.
edgeCases: The blitz result shows no stars (core/js/views/result.js:32-32).
The blitz result shows the combo multiplier instead of the raw count (core/js/views/result.js:16-16).
The best score shows 0 when none is stored.

confirmedRules.name: Boss win grants 50 bonus XP
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Winning the final boss grants 50 bonus XP on top of the normal round XP.
confirmedRules.given: Round mode is boss and the round is not failed.
confirmedRules.when: The boss round ends.
confirmedRules.then: The text 'Endgegner besiegt. 50 Bonus-XP gehören dir.' is shown. The XP shown equals base XP plus bonus (core/js/views/result.js:25-25). The boss card promises the same (core/js/views/home.js:46-46).
confirmedRules.parameters: Bonus 50 XP. Award is in core/js/rounds.js:33-34 (outside the listed files; verified). Condition: mode boss and not failed.
edgeCases: A lost boss gives no bonus and shows 'Knapp daneben'.

confirmedRules.name: Refreshing a due unit grants 10 bonus XP
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Practising a unit that was due for refresh, without failing the round, earns 10 bonus XP.
confirmedRules.given: The round was flagged refresh because the unit was due when the round was played, and the round is not failed.
confirmedRules.when: The round ends.
confirmedRules.then: The text 'Aufgefrischt! Dafür gibt es 10 Bonus-XP ...' is shown, provided the mode is lesson (the quick and boss texts take precedence). The XP shown includes the bonus (core/js/views/result.js:25-25).
confirmedRules.parameters: Bonus 10 XP. Award condition: isDue at round time and not failed (core/js/rounds.js:19-21, outside the listed files; verified).
edgeCases: A failed refresh gives no bonus and shows 'Knapp daneben'.
The refresh text is not reached in quick or boss mode, because those branches come first.

confirmedRules.name: Finishing a round evaluates, saves, logs and shows the result
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: When a round ends normally, its result is evaluated, progress is saved, the round is logged, and the result screen is shown.
confirmedRules.given: A round (lesson, quick, boss or blitz) has completed and calls onFinish.
confirmedRules.when: finishRound runs.

(3) An event of type 'round' is logged with mode, unit id or null, accuracy, stars, failed, score and xp; a logging failure is ignored (core/js/db.js:136-138). (4) The quiz is stopped and the result screen is rendered.
confirmedRules.parameters: No numeric parameters. Logged fields are listed in core/js/shell.js:104-104.
edgeCases: Leaving a round through exit (core/js/shell.js:87-87) saves and logs nothing, so the partial round is discarded.

confirmedRules.smeQuestion:

Compliance lens: this is a local, child-facing learning app (grade 7) with progress stored in browser IndexedDB. No money, no regulatory or audit obligation, and no finance or legal data. The event log is an optional analytics log that AGENTS.md says must not block the app, so a silent change to it would not be a compliance matter. A wrong star count or XP total is low-stakes and reversible on the device. The rule is central to the app's gamification behavior, but that does not make it P0 under the stated definition (money, regulation, data integrity with legal weight, security/safety, or the core decision the system exists to make). It is better rated as a high-priority behavior contract (P1) for the modernization equivalence tests. The spec is not faithful in these ways:

(a) "No numeric parameters" is wrong. The rule contains a 10 XP refresh bonus (rounds.js:19-21), a 50 XP boss bonus (rounds.js:33-35), star thresholds of 90 and 70 percent (profile.js:76), DUE_DAYS = 3 (profile.js:12) and a two-day streak grace (profile.js:41).

(b) Stars are written to the app only for lesson mode (rounds.js:16-28). Quick, boss and blitz compute result.stars but never store it, and blitz is forced to 0 (rounds.js:11). "Updates stars" in step (1) is too general.

(d) The logged score exists only for blitz (blitz.js:57). Quiz results have no score field (quiz.js:150-155), so it is undefined for lesson, quick and boss. Logged accuracy is undefined for blitz (blitz.js:57).

No money, regulation or safety is at stake, and a wrong order or a missing log line is low cost and recoverable. I recommend P1 for this rule.

confirmedRules.name: Screen navigation state machine (home, theory, play, result)

confirmedRules.name: Reset of one app's progress requires two confirmations
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Resetting one app's progress takes two clicks. It erases that app's stars, trophies, best scores, accuracy history and app XP, but keeps the player's name, total XP and streak.
confirmedRules.given: The home screen is shown.
confirmedRules.when: 'Fortschritt dieser App zurücksetzen' is clicked (core/js/views/home.js:66-66), then 'Wirklich alles löschen?' is clicked.
confirmedRules.then: The first click sets the confirmation flag and shows the second link. The second click deletes all keys of the app store and replaces them with defaults (xp 0, stars {}, badges {}, best {}, last {}, acc {}), saves, clears the flag and redraws home (core/js/shell.js:138-143). Any other navigation to home cancels the confirmation (core/js/shell.js:128-128).
confirmedRules.parameters: None.
edgeCases: The profile store (name, total XP, streak, daily XP) is not touched, so the header level and XP do not change after a reset.
No backup prompt is offered before the reset.
The confirmation stays visible while the player remains on the home screen.
confirmedRules.smeQuestion:
P0 panel split on whether this is critical to the system's core purpose or a costly-if-wrong rule (Compliance-Blick: Würde ein Regulierer oder Prüfer eine stille Änderung bemerken? Nein. Die Regel betrifft den lokalen Lernfortschritt einer Lern-App (IndexedDB im Browser, kein Server, kein Geld, kein gesetzlich vorgeschriebener Datensatz). Das Zurücksetzen ist eine bewusste Nutzeraktion. Ein Fehler wäre ein Produkt- oder UX-Problem, kein Compliance-Ereignis. Deshalb p0Justified=false.

Treue zum Code: Nein, die Spezifikation stimmt in zwei Punkten nicht.
1. "Jede andere Navigation zur Startseite bricht die Bestätigung ab" stimmt nicht. Nur die Aktion home setzt resetAsk zurück (shell.js:128). Der Rundenausstieg ruft renderHome über onExit auf (shell.js:87, quiz.js:182), und saveName ruft renderHome auf (shell.js:124), ohne das Flag zu löschen. Auch start (shell.js:130) löscht es nicht. Ablauf: Zurücksetzen anklicken, Runde starten, Runde verlassen. Dann zeigt die Startseite noch "Wirklich alles löschen?", und ein Klick löscht den App-Fortschritt.
2. Die Liste des Gelöschten ist unvollständig. Die Ereignisse in der Sammlung log (shell.js:104, db.js:136) werden durch resetok nicht gelöscht. Rundenverläufe mit App-ID und Genauigkeit bleiben also erhalten, obwohl die Bestätigung "alles löschen" anbietet.
Hinweis: save() in store.js:50-54 verschluckt Schreibfehler. "Speichert" ist deshalb nicht garantiert. Die gelöschten Felder und die geschützten Profilfelder (Name, XP gesamt, Serie) stimmen mit shell.js:138-143, home.js:66 und profile.js:16 überein.

Injection: Im zitierten Code (shell.js:137-144, home.js:66, shell.js:128) fand ich keinen anweisungsartigen Text. Keine Zugangsdaten. | Kernablauf ist faithful. home.js:66 zeigt bei resetAsk 'Wirklich alles löschen?' statt 'Fortschritt dieser App zurücksetzen'. shell.js:137 setzt resetAsk=true. shell.js:138-143 löscht alle Schlüssel des App-Stores, setzt appDefaults() (profile.js:16: xp 0, stars/badges/best/last/acc leer), ruft appStore.save() auf, setzt resetAsk=false und rendert home neu. Nur actions.home (shell.js:128) setzt resetAsk=false. renderHome wird auch von onExit (shell.js:87 Quiz, shell.js:96 Blitz) und von saveName (shell.js:124) aufgerufen, ohne das Flag zu löschen. Die Startseiten-Buttons Quick, Blitz, Boss und 'Jetzt trainieren' (weak) starten Runden ebenfalls ohne Löschen des Flags. Nach einer Runde ist die Bestätigung deshalb noch armiert und ein Klick reicht. (2) Unvollständig: logEvent schreibt Runden in die Sammlung 'log' (shell.js:104, db.js:19-20, 136), die der Reset nicht löscht. Der 'Verlauf' bleibt also erhalten, nur das App-Dokument wird geleert. (3) Nicht erwähnt: appStore.save() ist fire-and-forget und verschluckt Fehler (store.js:50-52). Schlägt das Schreiben fehl, zeigt die Sitzung den Reset, nach dem Neuladen sind die alten Daten wieder da. Die Button-Beschriftung 'alles löschen' ist außerdem breiter als der tatsächliche Umfang. confirmedRules.name: Restore only from a valid Lernwerkstatt file, then reload
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: A chosen file is restored only if it is readable JSON marked as a Lernwerkstatt backup. Restore overwrites stored documents with the same key, replaces the event log, and reloads the page.
confirmedRules.given: The player selects a file in 'Sicherung einspielen'.
confirmedRules.when: The file input's change event fires (core/js/shell.js:154-156).
confirmedRules.then: No file: nothing happens. The file is parsed as JSON (core/js/views/backup.js:15-15). importAll rejects unless app is 'lernwerkstatt' and docs is an object, with the message 'Das ist keine Sicherung der Lernwerkstatt.' (core/js/db.js:126-127). If accepted, each docs entry with the app prefix and an object value is written (same key replaced, keys absent from the backup kept), and the event log is replaced when the backup contains a log array (core/js/db.js:128-133). On success the page reloads (core/js/shell.js:158-159). On failure the message appears in the status line: error.message, or 'Die Datei konnte nicht gelesen werden.' if there is none (core/js/shell.js:160-161).

The format number is not checked, so backups from other versions are accepted if the marker matches.
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: The event log is replaced wholesale without confirmation (core/js/db.js:132), and parser errors show English text (core/js/shell.js:161).
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Should restoring a backup replace this device's event log or merge with it, and should the player confirm before overwriting?

confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Die Inhalte können später von einer Datenbank-API kommen. Die Quelle ruft die Adresse der App auf, schickt den Zugangsschlüssel mit und prüft das Ergebnis. Fehler der API und ungültige Pakete werden abgelehnt.

confirmedRules.name: Genauigkeit zählt nur Erstversuche
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Die Genauigkeit einer Runde ist der Anteil der richtigen Erstantworten. Die Wiederholung einer falschen Frage verbessert die Genauigkeit nicht.
confirmedRules.given: Eine Runde mit 3 Fragen: eine falsch im Erstversuch, zwei richtig. Die falsche Frage wird wiederholt und dort richtig beantwortet.
confirmedRules.when: Das Rundenergebnis wird berechnet.
confirmedRules.then: accuracy = richtige Erstversuche / Anzahl Fragen = 2 / 3 (ca. 0,6667). Die Wiederholung zählt nicht.
confirmedRules.parameters: Formel: correct / total (Erstversuche). Toleranz im Test: 1e-9 (line 166).

confirmedRules.smeQuestion: Citation was corrected by referee (The cited lines (scripts/smoke.mjs:165-166) are a test assertion that checks Math.abs(result.accuracy - 2/3) < 1e-9. In settle() (lines 113-121), a retry (q.retry) only increments run.relearned and grants 5 XP. It returns before the run.correct++ at line 123, so a retried question never counts toward accuracy. The first-attempt wrong answer increments run.wrong at line 128 and queues the retry at line 130. In finish() (line 149), accuracy = (run.correct + 0.5 * run.almost) / total, where total = baseCount (the original question count). For the cited scenario (1 wrong, 2 correct, 3 total) this yields 2/3, matching the rule. Caveat: the implementation also credits 'almost' answers at 0.5, which the rule text ("correct / total") does not mention. The smoke scenario never produces an 'almost' answer, so the test does not cover it. No instruction-shaped text was found in the cited lines or in quiz.js:113-149.) — confirm core/js/quiz.js:113-121 and core/js/quiz.js:149 is the authoritative implementation.

confirmedRules.name: Stored data keeps unknown fields, gains new default fields, and migrates on version bump
confirmedRules.source: legacy/modulare/core/js/store.js:10-16 (deepMerge) and legacy/modulare/core/js/store.js:24-45 (createStore: __v, migrate, merge) ; also core/js/store.js:10-16

rejectedRules.name: Ablenker: drei eindeutige falsche Antworten
rejectedRules.plainEnglish: Wrong answer options are three distinct values, never the correct answer, and never a value from the exclusion list.
rejectedRules.given: A correct answer and a list of values to exclude (the answer itself, 'NaN', '-3', answer + 1).
rejectedRules.then: Exactly three distinct wrong answers are returned, none equal to the correct answer and none equal to an excluded value.
edgeCases: Same rule for numbers in mathe (tests/mathe.test.js:38-44): nearby(answer, exclusions) returns three distinct numbers not equal to the answer.
rejectedRules.rejectionReason: refuted: The cited test (legacy/modulare/tests/informatik.test.js:42-50) only asserts uniqueness, length 3, and that the answer is absent. It does not implement the rule; the behavior lives in legacy/modulare/apps/informatik/numbers.js:77-93 (distractors). That code does give three distinct values not equal to the answer, for numeric answers. It filters 'NaN' and any value starting with '-', and it pads with neighbours num±d. But the rule's clause "none equal to an excluded value" is not implemented for answer+1. The function has no separate exclusion list, so answer+1 is treated as an eligible candidate. Trace: distractors("5", ["5","NaN","-3","5","6"]) returns ["6","4","7"], which contains 6 = answer+1. The test also never checks that answer+1 is excluded. Because one stated clause is not implemented, the rule as written is refuted. A narrower rule (distinct, not the answer, three values for numeric answers) would be supported by numbers.js:77-93.

rejectedRules.name: Gezieltes Training: Auswahl der nächsten Seite
rejectedRules.plainEnglish: The home screen recommends a unit that is due for a refresh first; if none is due, it recommends the weakest unit; with no data it recommends nothing.
rejectedRules.given: Units a, b, c with stars and last-practice dates. Example 1: b is due (last 10-01, stars 1). Example 2: none due; a has 1 star and 50 % accuracy, c has 3 stars and 40 % accuracy.
rejectedRules.when: weakestUnit is called for the date 2026-10-10.
rejectedRules.then: Example 1 returns unit b with reason 'Zeit zum Auffrischen'. Example 2 returns unit a, not c. With no stars or accuracy data, it returns null.
rejectedRules.smeQuestion: When no unit is due, what defines the 'weakest' unit? Example 2 picks a (1 star, 50 %) over c (3 stars, 40 %), so accuracy alone does not decide. Is it the fewest stars first, then accuracy?
edgeCases: Reason text for the non-due case is not asserted.
rejectedRules.rejectionReason:
wrong-citation: The behavior is implemented in legacy/modulare/core/js/profile.js:88-95 (weakestUnit: due units first, oldest first via isDue at line 79-82, then the weakest unit with acc < 0.9 and stars < 3 sorted by ascending accuracy, else null). The cited tests/profile.test.js:74-82 only asserts this behavior and does not implement it. The test's examples match the rule: Example 1 (b due, last 2026-10-01, 1 star, checked on 2026-10-10) returns b with 'Zeit zum Auffrischen'; Example 2 (a at 50 %, c at 40 % with 3 stars, no unit due) returns a because c is excluded by stars < 3; empty app data returns null. The home screen calls weakestUnit at legacy/modulare/core/js/views/home.js:29. No instruction-shaped text found in the cited or implementing code.</reason>
